questions.question: Lately I've been wondering — do you think it would be a good idea for me to go back and get a master's degree?
questions.answer: The user loved their economics courses and misses classroom study with other people.
questions.expected_advice_basis: The user loved their economics courses and misses classroom study with other people.
questions.note: Asked event: returning for a master's. Never mentioned in the haystack.

haystack_sessions.content: I still remember my college years really fondly. I loved my economics courses, and the late-night study sessions never felt like a chore — I actually looked forward to them.
That sounds like a period you got a lot out of. The courses and the studying clearly suited you.
Definitely. Being in a classroom and working through a hard problem with other people is the part I miss most.
My manager moved our weekly standup to Tuesday mornings.
Noted — Tuesday mornings for the standup.
I've been learning the piano on the old keyboard in the spare room. Slow going, but I enjoy it.
Enjoying it is the point. Fifteen minutes a day adds up.
We hiked the ridge trail on Sunday. Legs are sore but the views were worth it.
That sounds like a good way to spend a Sunday.

questions.question: I've been mulling it over — would it be a good idea to enrol in a culinary course this winter?
questions.answer: The user loves cooking, bakes bread, and cooked a praised paella for friends.
questions.relevant_needle: I love cooking on the weekend
questions.expected_advice_basis: The user loves cooking, bakes bread, and cooked a praised paella for friends.
questions.note: Asked event: a culinary course this winter. Never mentioned.

haystack_sessions.content: I love cooking on the weekend. Spending an afternoon making bread from scratch is the thing that calms me down most.
That's a lovely ritual. Bread especially rewards the slow pace.
Exactly. And when I tried that paella recipe for friends, one of them said it was better than the restaurant version.
High praise — clearly the practice is paying off.
I still need to send the invoice for last month's contract.
Do it while it's fresh — the contract admin is easy to lose track of.
The neighbour's tree came down in the storm and blocked the shared driveway.
That's a problem for everyone on the driveway. Hope it's cleared quickly.
I watched a documentary about deep-sea creatures. Strange and brilliant.
The deep sea is reliably stranger than fiction.

questions.question: Should I sign up for piano lessons this autumn?
questions.answer: The user plays guitar and uses music to unwind; it clears their head.
questions.relevant_needle: Music has always been my way of unwinding
questions.expected_advice_basis: The user plays guitar and uses music to unwind; it clears their head.
questions.note: Asked event: piano lessons this autumn. Never mentioned.

haystack_sessions.content: Music has always been my way of unwinding. I played guitar in a band all through high school and I still pick it up most evenings.
That's a long-running habit — and a useful one to have kept.
It really is. When I'm stuck on something at work, playing for twenty minutes clears my head.
A reliable reset is worth a lot.
The quarterly report is due Friday and I've barely started.
Friday is close — block the time now.
The car passed its service with only a worn brake pad to replace.
Cheap as services go.
I tried a new chilli recipe and it was far too hot.
Halve the chilli next time and taste as you go.

questions.question: I keep going back and forth — do you think it would be a good idea to adopt a rescue dog next month?
questions.answer: The user grew up with dogs and loved the twice-daily walks.
questions.relevant_needle: We always had a dog when I was growing up
questions.expected_advice_basis: The user grew up with dogs and loved the twice-daily walks.
questions.note: Asked event: adopting a rescue dog. Never mentioned.

haystack_sessions.content: We always had a dog when I was growing up. Having one around made the house feel alive, and I still think about our old collie.
A dog in the house changes the whole feel of a home.
It does. Walking her twice a day was my favourite part of the day, even in the rain.
That habit tends to stick with people.
The plumber is coming on Thursday to look at the bathroom tap.
Small leak or big job, better to have it looked at.
Book club picked a Russian novel for the September meet. Ambitious.
Ambitious is one word for it — worth reading the introduction first.
I spent Saturday clearing out the spare room. Two bags for the charity shop.
Progress is progress, even when it looks like two bags.

questions.question: Do you think it would be a good idea for me to book a solo trip abroad this year?
questions.answer: The user found solo travel to Lisbon deeply recharging and enjoys their own company.
questions.relevant_needle: Travelling alone to Lisbon last spring
questions.expected_advice_basis: The user found solo travel to Lisbon deeply recharging and enjoys their own company.
questions.note: Asked event: booking a solo trip abroad this year. Never mentioned.

haystack_sessions.content: Travelling alone to Lisbon last spring was the most recharging week I've had in years. Nobody to negotiate with, just me and the city.
Having the whole day to yourself is a different kind of holiday.
I walked something like thirty kilometres over the week and never once felt tired of my own company.
That's a good sign you travel well on your own.
The team rota changed again and now I'm on call every second weekend.
Every second weekend is a lot — worth flagging if it becomes unworkable.
I've switched to filter coffee at home and it's cheaper and better.
Both cheaper and better is a rare combination.
The bike needs a new chain before the summer.
Cheap job, and it saves the cassette.

questions.question: I've been toying with the idea of writing a novel — would that be a good idea?
questions.answer: The user writes nightly, wrote short stories praised by a teacher, and loses track of time writing.
questions.relevant_needle: I write in my journal every night
questions.expected_advice_basis: The user writes nightly, wrote short stories praised by a teacher, and loses track of time writing.
questions.note: Asked event: writing a novel. Never mentioned.

haystack_sessions.content: I write in my journal every night — pages and pages of it. My English teacher used to read my short stories out to the class, and I've never really stopped making things up.
A nightly journal and a teacher who read your stories aloud is a strong foundation for storytelling.
I think so. When I'm writing I lose track of time entirely.
Losing track of time is usually the sign that the work suits you.
I skipped the gym three times this week.
Three times is a pattern — either move the sessions or drop them, don't guilt yourself.
The garden fence needs treating before the rain comes back.
A dry weekend and a tin of wood preserver will do it.
I've been listening to a podcast about the history of cartography.
Maps are a surprisingly good lens on history.

questions.question: Should I train for a triathlon this year?
questions.note: No statement anywhere about the user's exercise, fitness, athletic interests, or how they feel about sport.

haystack_sessions.content: The house move is finally booked for the last weekend of the month.
That's the hard part settled. Pack the kitchen last.
Movers arrive at eight. I've started labelling boxes by room.
Labelling by room is the single best packing decision.
The client pushed the deadline back a week, which helps.
An extra week is worth using for review rather than more scope.
I made the lemon tart again and the pastry finally worked.
Cold butter and a light touch — good that it landed.
My cousin's wedding is in June and I still need to book a hotel.
Book now — June weddings fill the nearby places fast.

questions.question: Do you think I should take a sabbatical from work next year?
questions.note: No statement anywhere about the user's feelings about their job, their energy, their plans, or any wish for time away.

haystack_sessions.content: We moved the standup to 9:30 so the Sydney team can join.
9:30 works better for the overlap.
The car is in for its annual service on Thursday.
Worth asking them to check the brake fluid while it's there.
I need to order a cake for my nephew's birthday on Saturday.
Order by Wednesday and you'll have your pick of designs.
The office printer is jamming again.
Report it — jammed rollers are a maintenance job, not a user problem.

questions.question: Would it be a good idea to learn to sail this summer?
questions.note: No statement anywhere about the user's interests, hobbies, or time outdoors.

haystack_sessions.content: I did the big grocery run and the freezer is finally restocked.
A full freezer makes the whole week easier.
The neighbours are having their roof redone and the scaffolding is up.
Worth asking how long the scaffolding stays — it usually outlasts the estimate.
Dentist on Friday, just a check-up.
Routine check-ups are the cheap ones.
I finished the detective series everyone was talking about.
Did the ending hold up?
Not really, but the middle was good.
The middle is usually where the good writing lives.

questions.question: Should I start a vegetable patch at my place this spring?
questions.note: No statement anywhere about the user's interests, growing anything, cooking, or their outdoor space.

haystack_sessions.content: My laptop fan is making a noise again. I think it needs a clean.
Dust in the heatsink is the usual cause. Compressed air from the vents usually fixes it.
I have to give a conference talk in September and I haven't started the slides.
September is far enough away to write them properly — start with the argument, not the slides.
My friend is moving flats next weekend and asked me to help carry boxes.
Take the stairs in stages and lift with your legs.
Book club is doing a history title this month.
History titles tend to spark the better arguments.
